To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T-bet and NF-κB interact with each other and that this interaction inhibits NF-κB-dependent IL-2 transcription.
the T-box transcriptional regulator, T-betS, interacts with the RelA subunit of NF-κB and that this interaction represses IL-2 gene expression.
T-bet and the NF-κB RelA transcription factor interact to form a heterodimer that represses the IL-2 locus in developing Th1 effector cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of T-bet's function as a repressor of IL-2 gene activation in Th1 cells.
the regulation of IL-2 gene expression during Th1 development.
the molecular mechanisms that are responsible the regulation of IL-2 gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T-bet is required for the down-regulation of IL-2 in Th1 cells.
T-bet and the RelA transcription factors heterodimerize and that this interaction is required for the down-regulation of IL-2 gene expression in developing Th1 effector cells.
T-bet and NF-κB heterodimerization is a key mechanism for IL-2 repression in developing Th cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T-bet–RelA interaction and its subsequent phosphorylation of T-beth508 are critical for down-regulating IL-2 production and promoting Th1 differentiation in response to antigenic challenge.
T-bet and NF-κB cooperate with each other in the initial induction of IL-1, but later, T-bet and the RelA subunit of NF-κB antagonize each other in regulating the expression of IL-2.
phosphorylation of T-bets508 is a prerequisite for the heterodimerization between T-bet and the RelA transcription factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the repression of the IL- 2 gene in developing Th1 effector cells involves the interaction of T-bet with RelA and is mediated by T-betS 508.
the down-regulation of IL-2 expression in developing Th1 is mediated by the interaction of T-bet with RelA and requires T-bets508.
the T-betS488 residue is required for T-bet's repressor function in IL-2 transcription.
